title: Tenant Fairness Window and Adaptive Allocator for Burst Isolation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We continue to observe shoulder-surfing noisy neighbor patterns where short, intense tenant bursts (spiky token throughput) cause transient queue growth, KV cache churn, and kernel warmup costs that materially raise tail latency for co-located tenants. Current soft quotas and static lane assignments lead to either wasted reserved capacity or brittle hard-evictions.

Proposal summary: Implement a Tenant Fairness Window (TFW) scheduler and accompanying Adaptive Allocator to provide rolling throughput guarantees, graceful short-burst absorption, and enforced quota backpressure when necessary. The TFW is a time-windowed banking model (e.g., 60s sliding window) that tracks a tenant's delivered tokens and available burst credits. The Adaptive Allocator uses windowed usage + SLO feedback (p90/p99 latencies, queue length) to reassign fractional lane capacity and trigger preemptive autoscale suggestions before hard eviction.

Key features:
- Rolling throughput budgets: per-tenant throughput_guarantee and burst_window_sec define baseline rate and allowed burst credits.
- Soft-fence lanes: lightweight per-lane token buckets applied in the runtime path; lanes can be softened (best-effort) or hardened (enforced) by policy.
- Adaptive reallocation: proportional lane redistribution when observed usage deviates from commitments, using an exponential backoff for reclaimed capacity to avoid oscillation.
- Autoscale integration: when window consumption predicts sustained >x% oversubscribe for >t seconds, issue autoscale signals (suggested extra lanes/GPU groups) to Dedicated autoscaler before eviction.
- Quota enforcement: multi-stage enforcement (informational alerts -> throttles -> temporary tenant soft-isolation -> hard-eviction as last resort).
- Telemetry & observability: new per-tenant windowed metrics, eviction reasons, autoscale triggers, and fairness scores surfaced in Console and Alerts.

Why this is different from past approaches: instead of static hard-slicing we use a short-timescale rolling budget with feedback-driven allocation to allow transient efficient multiplexing while preserving predictable SLOs for committed tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Simulated noisy neighbor workload shows p99 latency for committed-tenants stays within SLO (<= 250ms additional tail) under 2x burst for 60s window
Autoscale signals are generated with <5s decision latency and successfully scale a canary Dedicated fleet in staging
Backend telemetry surfaces tenant_fairness_window_consumption, tenant_eviction_reason, and tenant_fairness_score in Console dashboards
End-to-end integration tests for throttle -> soft-isolation -> eviction transitions pass with deterministic rollbacks
No >5% throughput regression for non-target paths in unit and integration perf runs
implementation_notes: Runtime change: add lightweight token accounting per-tenant per-lane with O(1) amortized updates to avoid hot-path overhead
Control plane: maintain sliding-window counters and a small ML-free predictor to estimate sustained oversubscribe probability (uses EWMA)
Autoscaler hook: new API endpoint /autoscale/suggest with tenant, predicted_load, reason, and suggested_capacity fields
Billing: burst credits consumed should be instrumented for chargeback and clearly labeled in usage reports
Backwards compatibility: default behavior is off; customers opt-in per-dedicated-pool via new config flags in the Dedicated UI and API
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): deploy runtime + control-plane feature flags, run synthetic noisy-neighbor sweeps across model sizes
Phase 1 (internal canary): enable for internal tenant pool (redwood-internal) with strict telemetry and kill-switch
Phase 2 (selected customers): opt-in beta with 3 customers representing different workload shapes (chat, embeddings, batch infer)
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): enable default for new Dedicated pools, provide migration doc for existing customers
Rollback: instant control-plane opt-out + lane-level soft-disable that causes runtime to ignore TFW tokens
open_questions: What default burst_window_sec balances multiplexer efficiency vs SLO predictability? (60s proposed)
Risk of EWMA predictor oscillation under correlated bursts across tenants — do we need a cooldown/guard window?
How should prepaid vs postpaid billing models consume burst credits (should prepaid get higher burst ceilings)?
Should eviction penalties (e.g., temporary placement ban) be exposed as part of customer SLA?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: misconfigured defaults could throttle legitimate sudden spikes (e.g., model warmup) -> Mitigation: conservative defaults, per-tenant opt-out, and extensive staging sweeps
Risk: added runtime accounting might increase p50 latency -> Mitigation: microbenchmarks in runtime tree and offload heavier prediction to control plane
Risk: autoscaler thrash due to inaccurate short-term prediction -> Mitigation: add hysteresis and require sustained oversubscribe for >t seconds before scale actions
notes: Design reviewed with runtime and infra on 2026-02-20 — see review minutes in design doc
PM acceptance criteria aligns with project revenue goal to reduce customer-visible tail incidents by 30% for Dedicated customers
Coordination required with Billing and Console teams for new metrics and UI surfaces
